newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise on UES ADR, seen flat.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise on UES ADR, seen flat.

text.p: Leading Russian shares followed market bellwether UES up on Friday on an announcement late on Thursday that the national power company would issue American Depositary Receipts in two or three months, traders said.
But they said the market was not likely to keep pace with UES, which would stay strong next week.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 shares closed at 297.60 after 290.66 on Thursday. Total market turnover was $28.7 million.
"The market was very strong today, and the news about UES issuing ADRs led to big buys and moved UES up almost a cent," said Alfa Capital trader Mikhail Khaleyev.
UES rose with some fluctuations throughout the day to finish at $0.2262 after $0.2105 on Thursday.
Level one American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) would trade in place of existing UES shares on foreign exchanges. Share prices generally improve on ADR issues.
"I've seen good demand today and there hasn't been much stock around locally which is why it rose so fast," said Brunswick trader Gary Kinsey.
International longdistance telecom Rostelekom closed at $3.500 after $3.450 and oil company Surgutneftegaz rose to $0.704 from $0.685 on Thursday.
Khaleyev said regional power company Mosenergo, which rose to $1.257 from $1.235 on Thursday, moved up on the UES news, also.
"I've seen a little bit of buying from the U.S. in ADRs -- a little bit of blue chip action at the end of the week," Kinsey said, though he predicted only UES would continue appreciating next week.
"In terms of UES there does seem to real foreign demand. As stocks move up there seems to be some selling -- but not in UES," he said.
Dealers said most market activity next week was likely to stay range-bound.
